description: We find where — and when — on Earth to rehearse a specific Moon or Mars landing site. Analog Twin scans the whole planet for the same terrain and the same sunlight, using open NASA elevation and illumination data, and checks itself against the analog sites space agencies already use.
summary: Before anyone lands on the Moon or Mars, they rehearse on Earth, at sites mostly chosen by tradition. Analog Twin measures it instead: pick a landing site and it scans all of Earth's land for the places with the most similar terrain and the most similar sunlight, and tells you in which weeks of the year the light matches. It answers where to rehearse, and when.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Analog Twin shows Earth, the Moon and Mars side by side. Click any point on one of them and the other two light up with its closest "twins". For a lunar or Martian target, each Earth twin comes with a similarity score, the feature groups that match and differ, and the best weeks of the year to go there, when the Sun's height above the horizon is closest to what the target site gets.

HOW IT WORKS

We sample elevation models of all three bodies on the same ground scale and describe each location by the shape of its terrain: slope, roughness at several scales, relief, curvature and landform position. A search over this index returns the most similar places on another body. A solar-geometry model for each body gives the sunlight regime at any latitude, and a sliding window over the Earth year finds the weeks that best match the target. A small crew of AI agents then turns a target and its twins into a field-campaign plan, using only numbers produced by the engine, and lists what cannot be reproduced on Earth (vacuum, lunar dust, one-sixth gravity).

WHY IT MATTERS

The challenge notes that terrestrial analog sites are not well characterized. Analog Twin makes the choice measurable and repeatable for any landing site, adds the time dimension, and surfaces candidate sites that are not on today's lists.

LIMITS

Similarity is terrain shape and sunlight regime only, not geology or chemistry. The sunlight model ignores local horizons. Results are at landscape scale, not rover scale.

TOOLS AND USE OF AI

Python (NumPy, FastAPI), CesiumJS, Three.js. The code was written with Claude Code (Anthropic) under the author's direction, from a written specification, and the product uses Claude models for the campaign-planning agents. All numeric results (similarity scores, sunlight windows, rankings) are computed by deterministic code, not by a language model. The team image was generated with code, with AI assistance.
dataRefs: LRO LOLA lunar elevation model (Moon LRO LOLA DEM 118m)
MGS MOLA Mars elevation model (Mars MGS MOLA DEM 463m)
NASA Solar System Treks imagery (LRO WAC Moon mosaic, Viking MDIM 2.1 Mars mosaic)
